Definition: to lave (the whole or a part of a thing)
BiblicalUsage: Rachats is to wash — to lave the whole or a part, hands or feet or body. Aaron and his sons were washed with water at the door of the tabernacle before they were clothed; the priests washed their hands and feet at the laver so they would not die; and on the day of atonement the high priest washed his flesh in the holy place. Isaiah turns the rite into a command: 'Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes.'
TheologicalSignificance: What this says to me is that washing is the Bible's picture of cleansing from the outside in: the priests washed because they were coming near to God, and Isaiah says the washing that matters is the putting away of evil. And I believe the water of the laver points forward to the washing that only God can do — the clean heart He gives, not the hands we scrub.
